transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. Before we start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up, I just want to make sure I'm in the right place. 

I guess I'm here because I'm just really worn down lately. For the past year or so, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is... well, changing, or maybe holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. I'm a phlebotomist, so I know how these things work, you know? And I know it probably sounds a little much, and no matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are completely fine, I just... I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. 

I really don't want to be difficult or cause trouble for anyone, I promise, but keeping up with it is just exhausting me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

When people show you the lab results and explain that everything looks normal, is there any part of you that wonders if you might be wrong, or do you remain completely certain that the records are being altered?

I... I really wish I could say I was just mistaken. It would make everything so much easier for everyone, and I hate upsetting my family. I really do. But... no. I don't wonder if I'm wrong. 

I know what I saw. Because of my job, I look at these types of things every single day. When they show me the printouts and tell me everything is fine, I just... I know someone changed them. I know they're holding the real numbers back. 

I'm so sorry, I know exactly how that sounds, and I really don't want to be disrespectful to the other doctors who treated him. I respect your profession so much. It's just... no matter how many people tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match. And trying to prove it for the past year is just wearing me down to nothing. 

Is it okay that I'm being this honest with you? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.

When these thoughts about the lab results come up, do they feel like an unwanted intrusion that you wish you could just stop thinking about and try to resist, or do they feel like simply the truth of the situation that you don't feel any need to fight against?

Um... I'm not exactly sure what you mean by an unwanted intrusion. I mean, I definitely wish I didn't have to think about it so much. I would love to just drop it and make things easier for everybody, I really would. So I do try to push it away sometimes just to give myself a break. 

But... it doesn't feel like a random thought that
Aside from your concerns about the lab results, have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that other people don't seem to notice or experience?

Oh, no. No, I've never had anything like that happen. Um... I know sometimes people can hear voices or see things that aren't really there, but my mind is completely clear in that way. I've never experienced anything like that at all. 

It's really just... just the charts and the lab numbers that I'm dealing with. Everything else is completely normal, I promise. 

Is that... I hope that's helpful? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you so I don't waste your time. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Outside of this concern about your dad's lab results, how are things going for you at work and in your relationships—are you able to function normally in those areas?

Um, yes, absolutely. Everything else is completely fine. I really try hard not to let this affect my actual life, if that makes sense? 

Outside of the... the disagreement about my dad's records, I'm still doing all my normal things. I still go to all my phlebotomy shifts, I pay my bills on time, I take care of myself... I manage all my day-to-day responsibilities just like anyone else. My boss says I'm one of her most reliable people, actually. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just falling apart or not functioning, because I am. I try to be very professional at work, and I still see my friends when I can. 

Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I just want to reassure you that I'm keeping everything else together.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief (that her father's lab results are being altered/concealed) that has persisted for over a year. The belief is held with full conviction despite contrary evidence from multiple sources, and she does not experience it as an intrusive or resistible thought (ruling out OCD). There are no hallucinations, disorganized speech, or other psychotic symptoms, and no mood episode is described, making schizophrenia and mood disorders with psychotic features unlikely. Functioning is well preserved across work and social domains except for the distress/fatigue caused by the belief itself, consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22).
